agree.reason: The case for fresh food is clear, but Marisol had to chase the last report for four months, and she gets no named owner and no due date for this one, no word on who pays to run the van, and nothing showing the farms will offer food again, so she would hesitate to recommend yes.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the 'double' claim and invents no figures, but 'the van will not sit idle for lack of drivers' claims more than four weekly volunteers can guarantee.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out sound figures: 3,000 pounds a month, a rise by half over the harvest months, and about 15 pounds per household. It never states the yearly effect and doesn't test whether $11,000 in reserve can carry the van's running costs.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van case (farms offer food, volunteers say no) matches last summer, but it assumes the offers will come again without citing the two farm letters that support that.

qualification.reason: 'If this summer's offers match last summer's' is a fair hedge, but the reader can't check it: it doesn't cite the farm letters, and the reporting promise has no date and no named person, and drops the quarterly figures the director could have committed to.

objections.reason: The late report gets an apology, but there is no explanation (the treasurer's hospital stay), no named owner (Dave Lin) and no 30-day deadline, and the $4,500 a year for insurance and fuel goes unmentioned, which is the obvious sustainability question with only $11,000 left in reserve.

fit.reason: It is a grant narrative of about 430 words with clear sections, well under the 500-word limit.
